html:
In the app

Guided mode’s lesson 3 is this chapter: it checks that this lesson’s tags are made, that S1_Run exists, is called from MainRoutine and verifies, and then watches the line while you run it and ticks each result as it happens:

  • Press Start on the panel: Line_Run comes on and the Run lamp lights
  • Press Stop: Line_Run drops

A machine has one bit that says it is running, and everything else hangs off it. Make a routine called S1_Run (Logic → New Routine…) and give MainRoutine a single rung, JSR(S1_Run);. Then write these rungs in S1_Run.

Tags this lesson needs

Create these before you type the rungs (Verify reports any you miss as unknown). Tags from earlier lessons are not repeated.

TagTypeKindDescription
StartBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.9LogixPro I:1/0 · Start push button, NO
Line_RunBOOLbase tagSeal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)
StopBOOLalias of Local:3:I.Data.10LogixPro I:1/1 · Stop push button, NC (1 until pressed)
Batch_DoneBOOLbase tagThe large-bottle count has reached the thumbwheel preset
RunBOOLalias of Local:5:O.Data.8LogixPro O:2/10 · Run lamp
Label_ReqBOOLbase tagLatched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn

The rungs

How it fits together

Rung 0 is chapter 4’s seal-in with two extra conditions: XIC(Stop) rather than XIO, because the stop button is normally closed (pressing it makes the tag 0), and XIO(Batch_Done), a bit step 9 will set when the batch is complete. Until then it is 0 and the XIO passes. Rung 1 drives the run lamp whenever the line runs; the main conveyor is deliberately not here, because it steps (step 3), and the divert conveyor, the box conveyor and the shredder have rules of their own (step 8). Rung 2 is housekeeping: when the line stops for any reason, drop a label request that is in progress so the labeler’s head goes home (step 10 explains the request).

Notice what this routine does not do. A stopped line keeps the step in progress, the dwell’s time and every “done” bit, because the bottles have not moved: Start must carry on exactly where Stop left off, or the shift registers of step 4 and the bottles they describe drift apart. Step 11 has the check that proves it.

Run it

Run mode. Press Start on the panel: the Run lamp lights and Line_Run is 1 in Monitor Tags. Press Stop: it drops. Hold Stop while pressing Start: nothing, because the stop contact is open. That is the whole of step 1.

Try it

Give the Run lamp a flash while the line is stopped but the controller is in Run mode: a TON that resets itself (chapter 7) and XIO(Line_Run)XIC(Flash.TT) on a branch of the lamp rung. Then take it out again: the lessons assume the lamp means running.

rungs.head: S1_Run · Rung 0
rungs.comment: SEAL-IN: Start latches Line_Run through its own contact; Stop is a normally closed button (1 until pressed) so it breaks the seal; Batch_Done (step 9) also stops the line

pred.q: Start is on, Line_Run is on, Stop is on and Batch_Done is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Line_Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start (LogixPro I:1/0 · Start push button, NO) is on) or (Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on), Stop (LogixPro I:1/1 · Stop push button, NC (1 until pressed)) is on and Batch_Done (The large-bottle count has reached the thumbwheel preset) is off, the rung turns Line_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. XIC(Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when Stop is on.
  3. XIO(Batch_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Batch_Done is off.
  4. OTE(Line_Run) Output Energize does: turns Line_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Line_Run on, and Line_Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: S1_Run · Rung 1
rungs.comment: Run lamp whenever the line runs. The main conveyor steps (step 3); the divert conveyor (step 8, it stops when the packer's lower lane is full), the box conveyor and the shredder have their own rules
rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is on, the rung turns Run (LogixPro O:2/10 · Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Line_Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Line_Run is on.
  2. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: S1_Run · Rung 2
rungs.comment: Line stopped: drop a label request in progress so the head goes home. Nothing else is forgotten on purpose: a step in progress (Conv_Index) and the done bits stay as they are, because the bottles have not moved, so Start carries on exactly where Stop left off and the registers stay in step with the bottles. Step 11's end-of-line check would catch it if they did not

pred.q: Line_Run is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Label_Req is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Line_Run).

rungs.words: When Line_Run (Seal-in run bit (LogixPro B3:0/0)) is off, the rung unlatches Label_Req (Latched while the labeler is asked to apply; cleared at PadIn).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Line_Run) Examine If Open asks: true when Line_Run is off.
  2. OTU(Label_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Label_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Label_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

Stop.desc: LogixPro I:1/1 · Stop push button, NC (1 until pressed)

Batch_Done.desc: The large-bottle count has reached the thumbwheel preset
